items.how: Make the status settle on a real answer (ready or not yet ready) or show an error with a retry, and keep the Check if ready button usable. A spinner running for 2 minutes with the button greyed out must not be a possible end state.
items.why: o1.png and s1.png both show 'Checking...' with a disabled button and no message, so the reader cannot learn whether the book is ready. Both reviewers rank it first and mark the story broken. Note that shot.png, cited as story evidence, is 8 bytes and not a picture, so only o1.png and s1.png support this.

items.how: Put the Reserve button above the fold at 1366x768 (shorter form, or a sticky action bar), and keep the tab order reaching it quickly.
items.why: o2.png and s2.png show the form filling the window at 1366x768 with the Reserve button not on screen. The reservation still completes, so this slows people down rather than blocking them.

items.how: Give the reader view a way to collect, such as a Collect action or a pickup code or confirmation that the desk can act on, alongside the 'Ready at the front desk' status.
items.why: s3.png shows the reader view with 'no link or button to collect the book', and o-collect.png shows Collect only in the desk-staff view. The release goal says a reader can collect, so the story completes only when walked as staff, not as the persona.

sides.position: collect-book works (walked signed in as desk staff, where a Collect button exists)
sides.why: It walked the story as staff, not the reader persona the release goal names.

sides.position: a reader has no way to collect from the reservation page
sides.why: s3.png shows the missing action in the reader view, which is the persona and the stated goal.

items.how: Pick one label for the reserve action and use it on every page. The walk card and the o2.png heading say 'Reserve a copy', so use that.
items.why: o2.png shows the heading 'Reserve a copy' and o3.png shows the button 'Hold a book' for the same action. No picture shows both on one screen, but the two together support the complaint.
s4.png shows a fully loaded page and says it carries no timings, so the 'about ten seconds' claim is a feeling. The Captain decides whether to have it measured.

deferred.how: The Captain, or whoever owns the host Button, checks the declaration at x.d.ts for a prop or slot that can supply what was declined. The decline gave only a bare path and no prop name, and the declaration is outside this pass.
deferred.why: o agrees but gives only 'fine', and s cannot tell because there is no picture. i3 now asks for a reader collect action, so the decline may block that fix and should be settled with it.
Both reviewers agree with the deferral, but no picture shows a stale ready state. The only status defect shown is the stuck 'Checking...' in i1, so recheck staleness after i1 is fixed.

o disagrees ('blocks me') and s agrees. No picture shows a long label blocking anyone: o2.png shows the real problem as the button below the fold (i2), and o3.png shows a short 'Hold a book' label (i4). Fixing i2 and i4 covers what o describes, and the label length stays polish.
